fits.fact: Built for nano tanks of roughly 20–40 cm, with a clamp that takes glass up to 8 mm thick.
Shouldn't be used under an aquarium lid or cover.
With the separately sold C II Base stand, it can light Wabi-kusa bowls.
GreenDeal rates it best for tanks up to 45 cm and usable on tanks up to 60 cm, clamped to the rim.
Bách Khoa Aqua says the RGB version helps green and red plants grow and brings out shrimp colours.

usage.fact: Setup: install the My Chihiros app and create an account, clamp the light to the tank, pair it over Bluetooth, then set brightness and on/off times.
The head rotates 360° and the arm height can be changed, so you can tilt the light out of the way during maintenance.
The app gives a sunrise/sunset schedule and stepless dimming.
Quới Decor's warranty doesn't cover damage from drops or water.

issues.fact: Aquasabi reviewers say the clamp doesn't hold firmly: the light sits tilted under its own weight and wobbles.
One 2024 Aquasabi reviewer says the clamp cracked their tank glass.
Dimming isn't smooth: the first step is a big jump and light drops off sharply at the low end, and one reviewer said a firmware update didn't fix it.
Aquasabi's average rating is 3.5 out of 5 from 4 reviews. Reviewers like the colour rendering, brightness and app control.
Version differences: the white C II has 60 white LEDs at 16 W. The newer C II RGB has 40 RGB LEDs at 20 W and moves the Bluetooth controller from the cable into the fixture.
Warranty depends on the shop: 6 months at GreenDeal, but only 1 month at Bách Khoa Aqua and Quới Decor.
Both versions were out of stock at GreenDeal, and Thủy Sinh Tím said it was nearly sold out.

alternatives.model: RGB UV Mini 9 Pro clamp light
alternatives.why: Much cheaper Vietnamese option at about 440,000₫ on Shrimp Home (out of stock when checked). Shrimp Home gives no specs, and one review site says Week Aqua quality varies from unit to unit.

Premium nano light (15 W, about 1,300 lm, for rimless tanks of about 2–7 gallons). On a UKAPS forum, one owner of both lights preferred its diffuser and on-light controls over the C II RGB, but it costs more. I found no Vietnamese shop price.
The cheaper sibling (about 1,300,000₫ vs about 1,780,000–1,950,000₫ for the RGB) for anyone who doesn't need adjustable colour.
